body.text: In short:
A Russian cargo ship subject to US sanctions has been hit by drones in the Baltic Sea.
Finnish authorities say the attack was likely carried out by Ukraine and the vessel later drifted to Finnish waters.
Authorities in Finland and Estonia worry this is another sign of the war spilling to neighbouring areas.

A Russian cargo ship with links to the military has been hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea in what Finland said was likely an attack by Ukraine, with the vessel later drifting to Finnish waters.

The 16-member crew of the Sparta II evacuated to lifeboats, then to a nearby Russian ship, and was on its way back to Russia, Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told public broadcaster Yle late on Saturday, local time.

Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia's north-west Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of the Baltic region, leading to fears that the war was affecting NATO territory.
"It is likely that Ukraine … is behind [the attack]," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen told a press conference, adding it was not clear why the vessel had been targeted.

The ship, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defence Forces said, corroborating an earlier account by Russian officials.

The blaze was ongoing late on Saturday and Finland was leading the rescue operation as the ship was at anchor in its waters, although Russian vessels may eventually tow the wreckage home, Finnish authorities said.
A Russian helicopter was suspected of briefly violating Finnish airspace during the rescue operation, said Mikko Simola, commander of the Gulf of Finland Coast Guard.
War is spilling over
Helsinki said it had introduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland to protect civilians and allow authorities to operate if drones needed to be intercepted.

"The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said.
Swedish combat aircraft, operating under Finnish command, took part in safeguarding Finland's and NATO's territorial integrity following the incident, Sweden's Defence Minister Pal Jonson said.
Finland and Sweden are NATO's newest member states, joining the military alliance in 2023 and 2024, respectively, in response to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
"The consequences of fighting Russia's aggression have reached the Baltic Sea," Estonia's Prime Minister Kristen Michael.
"Another signal for the aggressor to stop. But nothing will stop us from supporting Ukraine."
Estonia sent a navy vessel to assist in the rescue operation, including firefighting and pollution response, its government said.
Ukraine's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Russia's embassy in Helsinki did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The vessel is subject to US sanctions and is linked to Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika, according to the US Treasury Department.
Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defence Ministry, according to the company's website.
"At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military material on board," Commander Iljin of the Finnish Border Guard said.
Russia says drones shot down over Leningrad region
Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that a cargo vessel had been attacked by two drones in international waters about 3 nautical miles from Russia's border.
Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region overnight.
Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks on the Leningrad region.
Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region.
Kaliningrad, which lies between Poland and Lithuania, has periodically been a flashpoint between Russia and NATO and the European Union.
Russia has previously described attacks on its commercial vessels outside its territorial waters as acts of terrorism and maritime piracy.
The attack follows Ukrainian strikes on the bridge linking Crimea to Russia.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky justified the repeated attacks, saying it was a a fair response to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Mr Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop".
"He wants a reason to escalate."
He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge, which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine, was "exclusively civilian" in use.
"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.
